arguments.content:
Caring for a Maltese dog's silky, white coat requires patience and the right technique to keep it luxurious and mat-free. With proper preparation and methodical attention, you can transform bath time into a bonding experience that yields show-quality results.

1. Gather all necessary products and tools before beginning, including a gentle whitening or moisturizing dog shampoo, a high-quality canine conditioner, cotton balls for the ears, a non-slip mat, a soft brush, a fine-toothed metal comb, slicker brush, high-velocity pet dryer, and several absorbent towels.
2. Brush the coat thoroughly while it is still dry, starting with the slicker brush to remove loose hair and surface tangles, then working through with the metal comb from skin to ends to ensure no mats remain, as bathing a matted coat will only tighten the knots.
3. Place cotton balls gently in the dog's ears to prevent water from entering the ear canal, which can lead to infections, and apply a drop of mineral oil to each eye if needed to protect them from shampoo irritation.
4. Wet the coat completely using lukewarm water, starting from the neck and working back toward the tail, ensuring every layer of the dense undercoat is saturated before applying any product.
5. Apply a small amount of gentle whitening or moisturizing dog shampoo, lathering it gently along the back, sides, belly, and legs, being careful around the face and avoiding the eyes and ears, then rinse thoroughly until the water runs clear.
6. Apply a high-quality canine conditioner, focusing on the longer hair on the body, legs, and topknot, allowing it to sit for two to three minutes to detangle and soften the silky strands before rinsing completely.
7. Squeeze excess water from the coat gently with your hands, then wrap the dog in an absorbent microfiber towel, blotting and pressing (never rubbing) to remove as much moisture as possible before blow drying.
8. Set up the high-velocity pet dryer on a medium heat and speed setting, beginning at the neck and working systematically toward the tail, keeping the nozzle moving continuously to avoid concentrating heat on one spot.
9. Use the slicker brush or metal comb simultaneously with the dryer, brushing each section straight as you dry it from root to tip, which helps straighten the coat and prevents new tangles from forming as the hair dries.
10. Once fully dry, give the entire coat a final thorough comb-through with the metal comb to check for any remaining tangles, paying special attention to friction-prone areas behind the ears, under the legs, and around the collar, then remove the cotton balls from the ears.

The entire bathing and drying process typically takes between 60 to 90 minutes, depending on the coat length and the dog's cooperation level. Consistent weekly maintenance using these steps will keep your Maltese's coat beautiful, healthy, and effortlessly elegant.
